newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 4.29 pct in strong recovery.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 4.29 pct in strong recovery.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted strong gains on Thursday in a continued recovery further buoyed by delayed payments ahead of a holiday, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 64 points, or 4.29 percent, higher at 1,556, recouping a total of 6.21 percent since Tuesday's 6.98 percent plunge caused by political worries and higher-than-expected January inflation.
Trade volume also rose to 33.80 trillion lira from Wednesday's 26.60 trillion.

Brokers said buying was encouraged by the holiday which caused Thursday's settlements to be delayed to next Wednesday and Friday's to next Thursday. Turkish markets will be closed next Monday and Tuesday due to a Moslem holiday.

"The recovery accelerated because yesterday's selective buys spilled over to most of the shares today. Political worries have eased and the market may again test the 1,700 barrier on Friday," said said Murat Aktas from Yasar investment.
The index had lost 13.82 percent by Tuesday's close from the January 27 all-time high closing of 1,700 after a 74.2 percent surge from end-1996. It has regained 6.21 percent since Tuesday.

Of the 239 shares traded, losers outdid gainers sharply by 212 to nine and 18 finished stable. The IMKB Industrial .XUSIN leapt 4.64 percent to 1,625, the IMKB Services .XUHIZ firmed 2.96 percent to 1,459 and the IMKB Financial .XUMAL rose 3.63 percent to 1,515.
Top actives were largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, up 1,000 lira at 22,500 and utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 217,500. They made up 19.6 percent of the total volume.
